cases.subject: The making of Hunminjeongeum, the new letters (1443-1446)
cases.location: The palace in Hanyang (no palace building named: not established for autumn 1446)

facts.statement: In the twelfth month of 1443 (Sejong 25), King Sejong himself made 28 new letters and called them Hunminjeongeum.

sources.title: 세종실록 102권, 세종 25년 12월 30일 경술 2번째 기사
sources.quote: 是月, 上親制諺文二十八字 … 是謂訓民正音。

sources.title: Memory of the World: Hunminjeongum Manuscript
sources.quote: the development of which he completed in 1443

sources.title: 상설전시 훈민정음, 천년의 문자 계획
sources.quote: 1443년 세종은 우리의 문자 '훈민정음'을 만들었습니다.

notes: The day is not given (是月, this month): only the year is used.

facts.statement: The book Hunminjeongeum, which explains the new letters, was completed in the ninth month of 1446 (Sejong 28).

sources.title: 세종실록 113권, 세종 28년 9월 29일 갑오 4번째 기사
sources.quote: 是月, 訓民正音成。

sources.title: Memory of the World: Hunminjeongum Manuscript
sources.quote: The manuscript published in the ninth lunar month of 1446

sources.title: 『훈민정음』[해례본] 개요
sources.quote: 1446년 음력 9월 상순에

conflict.note: The Annals' entry is dated the 29th of the ninth month ('this month'); Jeong In-ji's postface says the first ten days of the ninth month. The game says only 1446 and 'autumn'.

facts.statement: The book's explanation of the letters (Jejahae) says the five basic consonant letters copy the speech organs: ㄱ the root of the tongue closing the throat, ㄴ the tongue touching the upper gums, ㅁ the mouth, ㅅ the teeth and ㅇ the throat.

sources.title: 우리역사넷 사료로 본 한국사: 한글의 구성 원리 (제자해)
sources.quote: 牙音ㄱ, 象舌根閉喉之形, 舌音ㄴ, 象舌附上腭之形, 脣音ㅁ, 象口形, 齒音ㅅ, 象齒形. 喉音ㅇ, 象喉形

sources.title: 한국민족문화대백과사전: 훈민정음28자모
sources.quote: 초성의 기본 문자인 'ㄱ, ㄴ, ㅁ, ㅅ, ㅇ'의 다섯 문자는 각 문자가 발음될 때의 발음 기관의 모양을 본떠 만든 것

sources.title: 한박웃음 2020년 10월 제86호
sources.quote: 자음자의 큰 특징은 발음기관의 모양을 본 떠 만들었는데요

conflict.note: The 1443 Annals entry says the letters imitate the old seal script (倣古篆); the Jejahae says they copy the speech organs. The game says what the book (the Jejahae) says, letter by letter as it gives them: the tongue's root for ㄱ, the tongue on the upper gums for ㄴ, the mouth, the teeth, the throat.

notes: Rewritten 2026-11-04 for the redesign: Mission 2 names each letter's organ, as the Jejahae does.

facts.statement: The book says the three basic vowel letters copy the round sky (a dot), the flat earth (a flat line) and a person standing (a standing line).

sources.title: 우리역사넷 사료로 본 한국사: 한글의 구성 원리 (제자해)
sources.quote: 꼴이 둥긂은 하늘을 본뜬 것이다 … 꼴이 평평함은 땅을 본뜬 것이다 … 꼴이 섬은 사람을 본뜬 것이다

sources.title: 한국민족문화대백과사전: 초출자
sources.quote: 'ㆍ'는 하늘의 둥근 모양, 'ㅡ'는 '땅의 평평한 모양', 'ㅣ'는 '사람의 서 있는 모양'

sources.title: 한박웃음 2020년 10월 제86호
sources.quote: 'ㆍ'의 둥근 모양은 하늘이 둥근 것을 본떴고, 'ㅡ'의 평평한 모양은 땅이 평평한 것을, 'ㅣ'는 사람이 서 있는 모양을 본뜬 것입니다

facts.statement: In his preface the King wrote that he made 28 new letters only so that people could learn them easily and find them convenient for daily use.

sources.title: 세종실록 113권, 세종 28년 9월 29일 갑오 4번째 기사
sources.quote: 予爲此憫然, 新制二十八字, 欲使人(昜)〔易〕習, 便於日用耳。

sources.title: 상설전시 3부 스물여덟 자를 만드니
sources.quote: 그 어떤 백성이라도 누구나 쉽게 배워서 편히 쓸 수 있도록 만든 한글

conflict.note: The Annals print 欲使人易習 (one 人, 昜 corrected to 易); the Haerye edition is usually quoted 欲使人人易習 (everyone). The game says 'easy to learn, for daily use', true to both.

facts.statement: Jeong In-ji's postface says a wise person can understand the letters before the morning is over, and a slow person can learn them within ten days.

sources.title: 세종실록 113권, 세종 28년 9월 29일 갑오 4번째 기사
sources.quote: 故智者不崇朝而會, 愚者可浹旬而學。

sources.title: 상설전시 3부 스물여덟 자를 만드니
sources.quote: '슬기로운 사람은 아침나절에 깨우치고, 어리석은 사람이라도 열흘이면 배울 수 있는'

conflict.note: 愚者 is 'the foolish'; the game, for children, says 'a slow person'. The Annals read 不崇朝; quotations of the Haerye edition often read 不終朝: the same meaning.

facts.statement: The explanations and examples in the book were written by palace scholars: Jeong In-ji with Choe Hang, Bak Paeng-nyeon, Sin Suk-ju, Seong Sam-mun, Gang Hui-an, Yi Gae and Yi Seon-ro.

sources.title: 세종실록 113권, 세종 28년 9월 29일 갑오 4번째 기사
sources.quote: 集賢殿應敎崔恒、副校理朴彭年ㆍ申叔舟、修撰成三問、敦寧注簿姜希顔、行集賢殿副修撰李塏ㆍ李善老等謹作諸解及例

sources.title: Memory of the World: Hunminjeongum Manuscript
sources.quote: later explanations and examples by scholars of the Hall of Worthies

conflict.note: Gang Hui-an was of the Donnyeongbu, not the Hall of Worthies: the game says only 'the palace scholars', never a number or a name.

notes: Not used by any puzzle or reveal line: the game never says who wrote the book. Kept for the record; no approval needed.

facts.statement: The Royal Secretariat (Seungjeongwon) was the office that carried the King's orders out and reports in to him.

sources.title: 한국민족문화대백과사전: 승정원
sources.quote: 승정원은 조선시대 왕명의 출납을 관장하던 관청이다.

sources.title: 승정원일기 소개
sources.quote: 승정원은 조선시대 왕명의 출납을 관장하던 관청으로

conflict.note: Accounts date its founding differently (1400 / 1405); it stood in Sejong's time either way.

notes: Not used by the redesigned case (2026-11-04): kept for the record.

facts.statement: In his preface the King wrote that the speech of his country differed from China's and did not fit Chinese characters, so many common people who had something to say could not put it into writing.

sources.title: 세종실록 113권, 세종 28년 9월 29일 갑오 4번째 기사
sources.quote: 國之語音, 異乎中國, 與文字不相流通, 故愚民有所欲言, 而終不得伸其情者多矣。

sources.title: 상설전시 훈민정음, 천년의 문자 계획
sources.quote: 세종은 글자를 몰라 자신의 뜻을 제대로 전달하지 못하고 억울한 일을 당하는 백성들을 위해 한글을 만들었습니다.

facts.statement: The book says letters for stronger sounds were made by adding strokes to the basic ones: ㅋ from ㄱ, ㄷ and ㅌ from ㄴ, ㅂ and ㅍ from ㅁ, ㅈ and ㅊ from ㅅ, ㆆ and ㅎ from ㅇ.

sources.title: 우리역사넷 사료로 본 한국사: 한글의 구성 원리 (제자해)
sources.quote: ㅋ比ㄱ, 聲出稍厲, 故加畫 … ㄴ而ㄷ, ㄷ而ㅌ, ㅁ而ㅂ, ㅂ而ㅍ, ㅅ而ㅈ, ㅈ而ㅊ, ㅇ而ᅙ, ᅙ而ㅎ

sources.title: 한국민족문화대백과사전: 한글
sources.quote: 'ㄱ ㄴ ㅁ ㅅ ㅇ'의 다섯 글자를 만들어내고, 다음으로는 소리가 세어짐에 따라, 이 다섯 글자에다가 획을 하나씩 더하여 아홉 글자를 만들었다.

facts.statement: The book says the vowels ㅗ, ㅏ, ㅜ and ㅓ are made by joining the dot (ㆍ) with the flat line (ㅡ) or the standing line (ㅣ).

sources.title: 한국민족문화대백과사전: 훈민정음28자모
sources.quote: 'ㅏ'는 'ㅣ'와 'ㆍ', 'ㅜ'는 'ㅡ'와 'ㆍ', 'ㅓ'는 'ㆍ'와 'ㅣ'가 어울려서 이루어진 것이다.

sources.title: 우리역사넷 사료로 본 한국사: 한글의 구성 원리 (해설)
sources.quote: 이 셋을 기반으로 ㅏ,ㅗ,ㅜ,ㅢ 등의 다양한 모음을 만들 수 있었다.

notes: The dot sits above ㅡ for ㅗ, under it for ㅜ, right of ㅣ for ㅏ and left of it for ㅓ, as the letters themselves show; the game draws today's letters.

facts.statement: The book says letters are joined to make one written sound: ㆍ, ㅡ, ㅗ and ㅜ are written under the first sound, ㅣ, ㅏ and ㅓ on its right, and the last sound is written with the letters of the first sounds.

sources.title: 세종실록 113권, 세종 28년 9월 29일 갑오 4번째 기사
sources.quote: 終聲復用初聲 … ㆍㅡㅗㅜㅛㅠ附書初聲之下, ㅣㅓㅏㅑㅕ附書於右。凡字必合而成音

sources.title: 한국민족문화대백과사전: 한글
sources.quote: ' · '와 'ㅡ' 및 'ㅡ'를 가진 글자는 첫소리 글자의 밑에 쓰고, 'ㅣ'와 'ㅣ'를 가진 글자는 그 오른쪽에 쓰도록 하였다.

facts.statement: Some letters of the fifteenth century, among them the dot ㆍ (arae-a), ㆆ, ㅿ and ㆁ, are not used today.

sources.title: 기획 전시: 훈민정음과 한글 디자인
sources.quote: 15세기 당시에는 있었지만 말소리가 사라지면서 현대에는 남아 있지 않은 'ㆆ(여린히읗)', 'ㅿ(반잇소리)', 'ㆁ(옛이응)', 'ㆍ(아래아)'와 같은 글자가 있다.

sources.title: 한국민족문화대백과사전: 한글
sources.quote: 'ㆆ, ㅿ, · (ᄋᆞ)'의 이름은 지어지지 않았고 … 지금 쓰이지 않는

conflict.note: ㆁ (yet-ieung) is counted differently: its sound lives on at the end of a syllable, written ㅇ. The game names only the dot ㆍ as a letter not used today.

facts.statement: The name Hunminjeongeum (訓民正音) means the right sounds to teach the people; the sounds here stand for the letters.

sources.publisher: 국사편찬위원회 우리역사넷 (National Institute of Korean History)
sources.title: 세종어제훈민정음
sources.quote: 이 책에서 ‘훈민정음’의 뜻을 주석하기를 … 즉 ‘백성을 가르치는 바른 소리’라는 의미이다.

sources.title: 한국민족문화대백과사전: 한글
sources.quote: 세종이 한글을 만들 당시에는 ‘훈민정음’이라 불렀는데, 이는 ‘백성을 가르치는 바른 소리’라는 뜻이다. 이 때의 소리는 글자와 통한다.

sources.title: 한글의 명칭
sources.quote: “백성을 가르치는 데 사용할 바른 소리(글자)”라는 뜻이다.

notes: The oldest gloss quoted is the 1459 Worin Seokbo note. The meanings are those of the Chinese characters, not of the Hangul syllables.
English order for the game: 'the right sounds, to teach the people'. 'Teach the people the right sounds' is not used as the meaning.

facts.statement: The name Hunminjeongeum was also shortened to Jeongeum; Jeong In-ji's postface to the book already uses it.

sources.title: 세종실록 113권, 세종 28년 9월 29일 갑오 4번째 기사
sources.quote: 癸亥冬, 我殿下創制正音二十八字, 略揭例義以示之, 名曰訓民正音。

sources.title: 한국민족문화대백과사전: 한글
sources.quote: ‘훈민정음’을 줄여 ‘정음’이라고도 하였는데, 이 이름은 훈민정음 해례의 끝에 있는 정인지의 글에 이미 나타나 있다.

fiction: The rainy night in autumn 1446, the burnt paper, the book hall and the servants' cloth are made up.
Bun-i, Sora and Taek are made up; so are the copied scrap, the groups drawn in charcoal, Sora's lesson box, board and slate, and the King's ten-day test of ordinary people.
King Sejong is real, but everything he says and does in the case is made up. Two of his lines retell his real preface (h9, h5); none is a quotation of a record.
The four groups of the name were never lost: losing and finding them is this story's own event, and only Bun-i's paper is made up.
The name is written in today's spelling. The game claims no fifteenth-century Hangul spelling of it: the book's title is in Chinese characters, 訓民正音.
Bun-i's two groups sit one above the other on her paper: that is how her paper looks in the story, not a rule of the 1446 book.

puzzles.derivation: The King's words (his preface, h9): many people could not write what they meant. The scrap shows a writer who could only copy 門 from the gate sign, a bucket ring and drops of water lead away from the gate: someone who carries water, from the kitchen well. Taek's shape words pick the same place's group (훈; 혼 has its dot on top, 운 no lines on top; made up: the groups by the places).

whyNot.a: Scholars write Chinese characters well: none copies the gate sign, and that group has its dot on top.
whyNot.b: No bucket stands at the guard post, and that group has no lines on top.

puzzles.derivation: Taek names the group by the organs on Sora's board (the Jejahae's organs, h3): the throat ㅇ, the mouth ㅁ; the flat line is the earth (h4), with no dot ㅡ; no added line keeps ㅁ, not ㅂ (h10). Together they write 음, sound.
puzzles.whyOnly: Nine tiles, three used: each line of Taek's names one letter only, and the six others answer a misread organ, a dot, a standing line or an added line. Taek's order is one order.

puzzles.derivation: Group 1 is built from Sora's words: the teeth + 1 line ㅈ (h10), a standing line with a dot on its left ㅓ (h4, h11), the throat's ㅇ at the bottom (h12). Group 2 has no words of its own: it is the group on Bun-i's slate, Mission 2's clue (음). The paper reads 정음.
puzzles.whyOnly: Group 1's words allow one sound, one line and one place of the dot only; Group 2 is only what the slate held. Group 1 is at the top.

puzzles.derivation: Stage A: the King's three questions, shown evidence in turn: who wrote it, how after ten days (h5, h6), who the letters are for (h9): the copied scrap, so the people. Stage B: the name read by its meanings (h14): what the King wants to do is what Sora does for Bun-i, teach; the group for the people is the one Taek describes, 민 (mouth, standing line, tongue on the gums, h3); what he gives them is the right sounds, Bun-i's note.
puzzles.whyOnly: Nine tiles, four used: LEARN is Bun-i's part, not Sora's; GATE is the copied sign; 문 has a flat line, 만 a dot, 빈 an added line. The three questions give one order.

learningObjectives: Read why the King made the letters, and use it as a clue.
Match words for parts of the mouth, and for a stronger sound, with the letters they describe.
Read place words (on its left, at the bottom, one above the other) to build letters.
Read what each group means, and build the name by its meaning.

cases.subject: The building of Hwaseong Fortress and Jeong Yak-yong's lifting machine (1794-1796)

facts.statement: Hwaseong Fortress was begun in the first month of 1794 and finished in the ninth month of 1796.

cases.subject: The rebuilding of Gyeongbokgung under the Heungseon Daewongun (1865-1868) and its cost to the people

facts.statement: Gyeongbokgung burned down in 1592, in the Imjin War, and lay in ruins for a long time until it was rebuilt in the 1860s.

sources.title: 한국민족문화대백과사전: 경복궁
sources.quote: 1592년 임진왜란으로 궁은 전소되고 말았다. … 오랫동안 폐허로 남아 있다가

sources.title: 신편 한국사 37: 2) 서원 철폐와 경복궁 중건
sources.quote: 임진왜란 당시에 화재로 소진되고 말았다.

facts.statement: The rebuilding of Gyeongbokgung began in the 4th month of 1865 (Gojong 2), when an office for it was set up; the Heungseon Daewongun led the work himself.

sources.title: 신편 한국사 37: 2) 서원 철폐와 경복궁 중건

sources.title: 내 손안에 서울: 우여곡절 끝에 완공…궁(宮)금한 '경복궁 중건' 이야기
sources.quote: 경복궁의 중건 사업의 시작은 1865년(고종 2) 4월 2일 조대비의 하교에서 비롯되었다.

cases.subject: Yu Gwan-sun and the Aunae Market march for independence (March-April 1919)
cases.location: Aunae (Byeongcheon) Market and Maebong hill, near Cheonan

facts.statement: Yu Gwan-sun was a student at Ewha Haktang in Seoul; after student demonstrations, the schools were closed by order on 10 March 1919, and she went home on 13 March 1919.

sources.title: 한국민족문화대백과사전: 유관순
sources.quote: 학생들의 시위가 극심해지자 일제는 3월 10일 전국적으로 휴교령을 내렸고, 학교로 갈 수 없게 된 유관순은 13일 기차를 통해 고향으로 돌아왔다.

sources.title: 유관순 열사 (2019-02-28)
sources.quote: 1916년 지령리 교회의 샤프 선교사 추천으로 이화학당 보통과에 편입했으며 … 3월13일 고향으로 돌아왔다.

facts.statement: On 1 April 1919 (the first day of the third lunar month, the Aunae market day), Yu Gwan-sun and others led a march for independence of thousands of people at the Byeongcheon (Aunae) market.

sources.title: 한국민족문화대백과사전: 유관순

sources.quote: '아우내 장터 독립 만세 운동'은 1919년 4월 1일(음력 3월 1일) 유 열사와 김구응 선생 등이 주도해 펼친 비폭력 만세운동으로

sources.quote: 음력 3월 1일 아우내 장날에 시위운동을 벌여

facts.statement: A signal fire on Maebong hill gave the sign for the march: Yu Gwan-sun lit it on the night of the last day of March 1919, the night before the 1 April march.

sources.title: 한국민족문화대백과사전: 천안 유관순 열사 유적
sources.quote: 유관순이 3·1독립만세 당시 봉화로 거사신호를 알렸던 매봉의 봉화대까지 … 매년 3월 마지막 날에 봉화를 올려 유관순 열사를 기념하고 있다.

sources.title: 움켜 쥔 시신의 손엔 독립선언서… 아우내 만세운동 '진짜 주역' (2019-02-12)
sources.quote: 1919년 3월 그믐날 밤 유관순은 매봉산에 올라 봉화를 올렸다. … 거사 일로 정한 4월 1일 아침 아우내장터에는 전날 밤 타오른 횃불을 보고 장꾼을 가장한 군중 3000여명이 모여들었다.

conflict.note: The Academy of Korean Studies names the fire on Maebong as the sign but gives no date; the date (the last night of March, the night before 1 April) is the press account's and agrees with the yearly fire on the last day of March. The 24 other hills are in press only: the game shows 'more lights' in a made-up transition, never as a fact.

facts.statement: At the market that day, Yu Gwan-sun's father Yu Jung-gwon and her mother Lee So-je were killed.

facts.statement: Yu Gwan-sun was arrested as a leader of the march, held in Seodaemun Prison, and died in prison on 28 September 1920.

conflict.note: The sentence differs (the Academy: five years, then three on appeal; Newsis: seven): the game gives no sentence. The age '18' is a Korean-count age; the game gives no age.

fiction: Gyeongsun, Dong-il, Mr. Pyo, the stranger with the coin, the three school notebooks and the girls Sunja and Okhui are made up.
Yu Gwan-sun is real, but every word she says and writes in the case (her mixed-up plan, the 'no bell' line) is made up; none is a quotation of a record.
The wrong day going round the villages, the messengers' talk and the keepers' letter box with its dial lock are made up.
People walking to the market 'like shoppers' follows a press account, not a checked fact: it is said only inside Gwan-sun's made-up plan.
The keepers' notes in the box (Bun-i's of 1446, Mrs. Kang's of 1909) are the season's made-up story.

clues.text: Two of them say the same day.

puzzles.derivation: The note says two of the three messengers agree. Gyeongsun and Dong-il both say the first of April (the real day of the march, h2); Mr. Pyo, paid by a stranger, says the second.

whyNot.april_second: Only Mr. Pyo, the man the note warns about, says the second of April.

puzzles.derivation: The plan's lines, read for time words: the sign (a fire on Maebong hill, h3) the night before; people walk to the market in the morning; when the market is full, the march starts (h2).
puzzles.whyOnly: Each step's time word allows one place only (the night before, in the morning, when full, then the march), and the plan rules out the bell ('No bell. A bell is too loud.').

clues.text: A small water drop sits by her name.

puzzles.derivation: The note is in Hangeul only and has a small water drop. Sunja writes in Chinese characters; Okhui draws stars; only Gyeongsun's notebook has the water drop by her name. Made up: no history in this puzzle.

facts.statement: After the March First Movement, the Provisional Government of the Republic of Korea was founded in Shanghai in April 1919: on 10 April 1919 a Provisional Assembly met and named the country Daehan Minguk (the Republic of Korea).

facts.statement: Kim Gu reached Shanghai in April 1919; in August 1919 he asked to serve as the Provisional Government's gatekeeper and was made its police chief (gyeongmu gukjang), the first to hold the post.

conflict.note: Some press says April 1919; both public sources say August 1919. The game says August 1919.

facts.statement: The Provisional Government's police guarded the government, its leaders and its office, protected the Korean community in Shanghai, and watched for Japanese spies.

cases.subject: Yun Bong-gil and Kim Gu on 29 April 1932, and what that day meant for the Provisional Government
cases.location: Shanghai (the house of the breakfast is not named)

facts.statement: On 29 April 1932, at a Japanese ceremony in Hongkou Park, Shanghai, Yun Bong-gil, a member of the Korean Patriotic Organization, carried out an attack on the Japanese army leaders there.

sources.title: 윤봉길

Yun Dong-ju is real, but everything he says and does in the case is made up; none of his lines is a quotation, and no line of his poems is quoted or translated (only the book's title).

puzzles.derivation: Yun's words describe one thing on the desk: the thick book with a red spine. Under it is the folded note; its blue spot is 'not ink' but a drop of what Bun-i carried (Case 01): water, the keepers' mark.
puzzles.whyOnly: Only one thick book has a red spine; the ink is ruled out by 'not ink', and Bun-i's bucket held water. RAIN and INK have their own feedback.

puzzles.derivation: Yun's list (made up) and the keeper's card (made up) give the same copy (2 of 3: three copies, h3), the same friend (Jeong Byeong-uk, h3) and the same poems (18 + 1 opening poem: 19, h2); only the string differs, WHITE on the list and BLACK AND WHITE on the card. Yun said in M1 that his friend's copy had a white string, so the card's line is the untrue one; read with the card's last words (keys of these colours) it gives black and white keys, which M3 shows to be the hall's piano.
puzzles.whyOnly: Three of the four lines are word for word the same on both papers; only the string line differs, and its pair is the answer. Each agreeing pair has its own feedback, which repeats the fact it holds.

puzzles.derivation: The lock's rule (made up) puts two numbers side by side: the copies, then the poems in each copy, both read on Yun's list (M2, recalled here): copy 2 of 3, so three copies (h3); 18 poems and 1 opening poem, so 19 (h2). 3 and 19: 319.
puzzles.whyOnly: Three copies only (2 is the friend's copy's number, refused with its own feedback), and 18 + 1 = 19: no other number fits. 318 forgets the opening poem; 193 swaps the order (order feedback).

puzzles.derivation: The copy's pages are in the King's letters (M3), which King Sejong made for the people's own language (Case 01); the schools now teach in Japanese and Korean became only a choice subject in 1938 (h4). Yun's poems are in Korean (h5): the case's key fact, said again in the ending with the friend's family keeping the copy (h6) and the 1948 book (h7).
puzzles.whyOnly: JAPANESE is what the schools push, HANGEUL names the letters not the language, CHINESE is ruled out by King Sejong's reason, ENGLISH by the pages: each has its own feedback.

fiction: The keepers' notes of 1446 to 1941 in the box, Haesu's lines in its lid, Bitna's drawing and tiles are the season's fiction.
Bitna, the trunks, the month card, the radio's words, the office, the family room and the river steps are made up; how the news reached the office that day is not claimed.
Kim Won-bong is real, but everything he says and does in the case is made up; none of his lines is a quotation. His life after 1945 is outside the case.
Bitna's note dated 8.15 and the word 광복 on it are made up; what gwangbok means is fact (h5).

puzzles.derivation: The note names two things together: one leather strap, and a round brass lock. Only one trunk has both.

whyNot.two_straps: It has the round brass lock, but two straps: the note says ONE strap.
whyNot.one_strap_peg: It has one strap, but a wooden peg: the note says a round brass lock.

puzzles.derivation: Bun-i's note (1446) is fixed at the bottom and Miri's (1941) on top; the lid's three lines chain the rest: Seok, Okbun, Duri, Gyeongsun. The drawing has no water drop and is set aside.
puzzles.whyOnly: The three relations make one chain between the two fixed notes; no two cards can swap.

puzzles.derivation: The day of Japan's surrender is the fifteenth of August (h3). Bitna's card gives August as month eight; the month goes before the day: 8 then 15, 815.
puzzles.whyOnly: Only August is the month said; the day is the fifteenth; the month comes first: 158 or 581 are the right digits in the wrong order (order feedback).

puzzles.derivation: Gwangbok is 光 light and 復 to come back (h5): gwang, the opposite of dark, is LIGHT, spelled with the five tiles found in the missions. It is the day of Japan's surrender (h3), and the ending says liberation was the work of many: the Allies' victory and Koreans at home and far away (h4).
puzzles.whyOnly: The five tiles make one English word meaning the opposite of dark; the tiles are listed H, T, I, G, L so the letter never spells it.

learningObjectives: Read a description with two features (one strap, a round brass lock) and choose the thing that has both.
Put events in order from before, after, the oldest and on top.
Read a date in words (the fifteenth of August) and write it as numbers, the month first.
Read what gwangbok means and spell it in English: LIGHT.

realHistory.text: Korea's government in exile moved to Chongqing in 1940. There it made the Korean Liberation Army.
realHistory.junior: In 1940, Korea's Provisional Government moved to Chongqing, where it founded the Korean Liberation Army.
realHistory.master: In 1940 the Provisional Government relocated to Chongqing and founded the Korean Liberation Army there.

realHistory.text: Kim Won-bong worked for independence from 1919. In 1938 he formed the Korean Volunteer Corps in China.
realHistory.junior: Kim Won-bong worked for independence from 1919, and in 1938 he formed the Korean Volunteer Corps in China.
realHistory.master: Kim Won-bong worked for independence from 1919 and, in 1938, formed the Korean Volunteer Corps in China.

realHistory.text: In 1942 he joined the Korean Liberation Army. In 1944 he became a minister of the government.
realHistory.junior: In 1942 he became vice-commander of the Korean Liberation Army, and in 1944 a minister of the government.
realHistory.master: He became vice-commander of the Korean Liberation Army in 1942 and the government's minister of military affairs in 1944.

realHistory.text: On 15 August 1945, Japan surrendered to the Allies. The war ended, and Korea was free again.
realHistory.junior: On 15 August 1945, Japan surrendered to the Allies; the war ended and Korea was liberated.
realHistory.master: On 15 August 1945 Japan surrendered to the Allies, ending the war and liberating Korea.

realHistory.text: Gwangbok means the light comes back. Gwang is light; bok is to come back.
realHistory.junior: Gwangbok means the return of the light: gwang is light, and bok means to come back.
realHistory.master: Gwangbok means the light restored: gwang is light, and bok is to return.

realHistory.text: Liberation came from the Allies' victory and from many Koreans at home and far away. The Liberation Army was getting ready too, but Japan surrendered first.
realHistory.junior: Liberation came from the Allies' victory and from the long struggle of many Koreans at home and abroad. The Liberation Army was preparing an operation, but Japan surrendered first.
realHistory.master: Liberation owed much to the Allies' victory and to the long independence movement of Koreans at home and abroad; the Liberation Army's planned operation was called off when Japan surrendered.
